addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## tecweave
Tools provided by the Tecweave coordinator. Every call is authorized against your role and recorded in the project ledger.

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
I read all seven files plus the C originals they port (`lib/helper/readline.c`, `lib/helper/printfb.c`, `lib/Platinenmacher/parser/command.c`/`.h`, `config.c`, `error.h`) and hand-executed every test.

## Verdict: no compile errors and no failing tests found

I could not find anything that would fail `rustc` (edition 2021, stable, std), fail a `#[test]`, or fail the doctest. Specifics on the points you flagged:

**2. `dispatch` borrow reasoning (`/work/rust/crates/pm-parser/src/command.rs:246-266`) — correct as written.** `Invocation` holds shared loans on `(*self).cmd` / `(*self).args`; `self.entries[idx]` takes `&mut (*self).entries` via `IndexMut`. MIR borrowck's place-conflict analysis treats distinct fields of the same struct as disjoint, so this compiles. `self.cmd.clear()` at line 264 is after the last use of `invocation`, so NLL ends the shared loans first. The `position` closure at line 252 only takes shared loans, coexisting fine with the shared `self.entries.iter()`.

**3. Lifetimes — all sound.** `F: FnMut(&Invocation<'_>)` (line 101) is parenthesized `Fn`-sugar, so both elided lifetimes become higher-ranked (`for<'r,'s> FnMut(&'r Invocation<'s>)`) — same shape as the ubiquitous `Fn(&mut Formatter<'_>)`. The test closures `|i: &Invocation<'_>| log.record(i)` get the same higher-ranked signature because annotating the parameter forces late-bound elision, so they satisfy the blanket impl and `impl CommandHandler + 'a`. `self(invocation)` at line 104 resolves through `impl<A, F: ?Sized + FnMut<A>> FnMut<A> for &mut F`. `log.take()` while `parser` is alive borrow-checks: the captured borrow of `Log` is *shared* (`record(&self)`, interior mutability via `RefCell`), and `take(&self)` is also shared. Dropck on `Box<dyn CommandHandler + 'a>` is satisfied in every test and in the doctest because each `Log`/`Cell` is declared *before* `parser`, so `parser` drops first.

**4/5/6.** All `assert_eq!` operand types unify (`Result<(), Error>` vs `Err(Error::OutOfBounds)`, `String` vs `&str` via `impl PartialEq<&str> for String`, `Option<&str>` vs `None`). I traced every state-machine and readline test by hand — including the CMD_MAX off-by-one (9 real registrations fit, the 10th returns `OutOfBounds`), `"render\r\nrender\r"` → `("\nrender", "")`, `"set  a b \r"` → `("set", " a b ")`, `" render\r"` → `("", "render")`, and `"line one\r\nline two"` / `"ssid\npass\n"` / `"a\n\nb"` / `"Grünstraße\r\nnext"` — and all assertions hold. The one real doctest (command.rs:46-57) compiles and passes; the `error.rs:10` block is `ignore`d.

**7.** No unused imports, unused variables, unused `mut`, or dead code. `new_without_default` and `len_without_is_empty` are both satisfied. `needless_range_loop` does not fire on `fb[height * i + j]`; `ptr_arg` does not fire on `&mut String` because `push_str`/`clear` are used.

## Non-blocking nits (nothing here breaks the build)

- `/work/rust/crates/pm-parser/src/command.rs:270` and `:276` — the caps are on `chars().count()`, but C caps *bytes* (`CMD_LENGTH + 1` / `CMD_ARGS_LENGTH + 1` buffers). With multi-byte input, `cmd`/`args` can exceed the C limits in bytes, and the test at line 410 asserts `.len()` (bytes) `== CMD_ARGS_LENGTH`, which only passes because the input is ASCII. If byte fidelity is the intent, use `self.args.len() + c.len_utf8() <= CMD_ARGS_LENGTH`. Also `chars().count()` per character makes a line O(n²) (harmless at n=70).
- `/work/rust/crates/pm-parser/src/error.rs:3` and `/work/rust/crates/pm-parser/src/config.rs:11` reference `rust/PORTING.md`, which does not exist in the repo (`/work/rust/` contains only `crates/`). Prose-only, so no `broken_intra_doc_links` warning, but the pointer is dangling.
- There is no workspace manifest at `/work/rust/Cargo.toml`; `pm-parser` is standalone, so cargo must be invoked from `/work/rust/crates/pm-parser`. Worth adding a workspace root before more crates land.
- `/work/rust/crates/pm-parser/src/error.rs:10` uses ```` ```ignore ````, which surfaces as an *ignored doctest* in `cargo test` output. ```` ```text ```` would keep the output clean.

input.message:
pm-parser: port command parser, config stub, readline and printfb

Ports into rust/crates/pm-parser:

* command.rs  <- lib/Platinenmacher/parser/command.{c,h}
  State machine kept byte for byte (\r dispatches, first space switches to
  args, later spaces are args, CMD_MAX counts the unknown slot). The C
  callback table becomes a CommandHandler trait blanket-implemented for
  FnMut(&Invocation), so closures register directly. Deviations, all
  documented in the module header: no putchar() echo (console I/O and the
  save_printf semaphore stay in the firmware task), no buffer overflow
  (over-long names/args are truncated at the C byte limits instead of
  smashing the heap), and no strcmp(NULL, ..) against the zeroed unknown
  entry.
* config.rs   <- lib/Platinenmacher/parser/config.{c,h}
  The C config_parser() is an empty stub; the port keeps that contract
  rather than inventing a parser.
* readline.rs <- lib/helper/readline.c
  readline()/countline() keep the cursor-in, cursor-out shape and the
  quirks the firmware relies on: \r is skipped rather than terminating,
  a source with no \n yields the trailing text with a None cursor, and
  countline() still returns 0 when there is no newline.
* printfb.rs  <- lib/helper/printfb.c
  Formats into a String or a fmt::Write sink instead of printf()-ing, and
  rejects a short buffer instead of reading past its end.
* error.rs    mirrors error_code_t until pm_core::Error lands; swapping it
  for `pub use pm_core::Error;` is a one-line change.

Tests: the four readline cases from test/host/Platinenmacher/test_helper/test.c
(identical to test/embedded/test_helper/test_sd_readline.c) are ported
verbatim, plus coverage for the command state machine (two registered
commands, unknown fallback, empty line, argument spacing, truncation,
CMD_MAX, duplicate names, CRLF) and for printfb geometry.

No C file is touched.
